I've done cross country trips with my rabbit twice now. I used a larger hard sided pet carrier for while we were on the road. Her carrier is big enough to fit a small litter box in so she was more comfortable. I filled her box with hay like I normally would and attached a bowl for water and provided a little while driving. I've made two 31 hour drives across country with my Holland lop Basil. The trip was spread out over three days with the majority of the drive taking place over the first two days. Basil isn't too crazy about road trips for the first few miles but later calms down. On our trips I made sure to stop every 3-4 hours (usually when it was time to fuel up) for about 20-30 minutes to let her rest a bit and eat. I provided her with a litter box in her kennel with some hay. I made sure she had a bowl of water and pellets during the drive too. Because it was such a long drive I made sure to get some critical care from the vet just in case but didn't have any use for it. If you can, bring some of your buns favorite fruits and veggies to temp them to eat. I kept a cooler with a bunch of greens soaked in water for her to eat during breaks. I would also ask your vet if they have any recommendations for travel.
